Q: `~` (tilde) operator in Boolean Full-Text Search in MySQL is not behaving as stated in MySQL developer website A:

Thank you for the detailed write-up, it is incredible that there is so little documentation on this topic.

I have been experimenting with this exact functionality, but I am facing the issue, that adding ~term will actually boost the rows with term instead of demoting it. I was wondering if anybody have experienced this issue, as I simply cannot find any similar cases online. Thanks!

Below is my exact results and queries. The data are job titles in Danish:

SELECT title, score FROM
    (
        SELECT title, MATCH(title) AGAINST
        ('pædagog' IN BOOLEAN MODE) AS score
        FROM jobs ORDER BY score DESC
    ) AS temp WHERE score != 0;

Returns the expected scores. Let's focus on demoting the last row.

# Title Score
0 Angerlarsimaffik Uulineq søger Pædagog og Socialassistent 2.791787
1 Pædagog til moderne daginstitution i børnehaveafdeling 2.791787
2 Pædagog til vuggestueafdeling med fokus på natur og udeliv. 2.791787
3 Pædagog til døgnafdeling - Livsværk 2.791787
4 Pædagog til SFO og indskoling på Vadgård Skole 2.791787

I am adding ~SFO to demote the last row. Note, that this behaviour is also seen, when using longer words, like ~børnehaveafdeling on other rows.

SELECT title, score FROM
    (
        SELECT title, MATCH(title) AGAINST
        ('pædagog ~SFO' IN BOOLEAN MODE) AS score
        FROM jobs ORDER BY score DESC
    ) AS temp WHERE score != 0;

This will boost the score for some reason...

# Title Score
0 Pædagog til SFO og indskoling på Vadgård Skole 8.273522
1 Angerlarsimaffik Uulineq søger Pædagog og Socialassistent 2.791787
2 Pædagog til moderne daginstitution i børnehaveafdeling 2.791787
3 Pædagog til vuggestueafdeling med fokus på natur og udeliv. 2.791787
4 Livsværk Pædagog til døgnafdeling - Livsværk 2.791787

The exact same behaviour is seen, if I use +pædagog <SFO and other combinations, which gave negative scores in the original post. Any insights would be greatly appreciated! I am using MySQL version 8.0.40

Q: Compiling OpenCV in C++ A:

I think that the accepted answer is a bit old.

At least for OpenCV 4.X, the most recently release today, you can use:

#include <opencv2/opencv.hpp>

and compile your program by something like:

g++ your_program_file.cpp -o your_program `pkg-config --cflags --libs opencv4`

Note opencv4 and not only opencv.

For example, using the command above to compile the following your_program_file.cpp file:

#include <opencv2/opencv.hpp>

int main() {

    std::cout << "The current OpenCV version is " << CV_VERSION << "\n";

    return 0;

}

And running:

./your_program

Outputs:

The current OpenCV version is 4.4.0

Which indeed matches with my current OpenCV settings.

Q: Why can't I change gcc compiler from 4.2.1 to later version? A:

The system gcc-4.2.1 compiler is a (very old) legacy of the migration from the gcc to clang compilers. It should never be used for your own code. Edit your .profile or .tcshrc to prepend the newer gcc directory to the path. Or save a lot of time and energy and use MacPorts.

Unfortunately, Clang has established 'absolute' compatibility at gcc-4.2.1: see: clang -E -dM - < /dev/null | grep GNU

That's not a bad thing. Once the compiler gains traction it's going to provide it's own extensions, and no longer track those of others. Many extensions remain compatible like Intel's <x86intrin.h>. It's not really in either compiler's interests to provide too much divergence with extensions...

The 'stable' gcc is now 8.2.0 according to MacPorts. The stable MacPorts clang (which irritably conflicts with OS X) is apparently 7.0.0 ... short story - don't go replacing sets of files arbitrarily that you think might work. Then set up paths correctly - IIRC, MacPorts will do this for you.

I provided a more recent summary: here.
